fields.prompt:
(2 points) Order the following layers of the atmosphere from lowest to highest altitude:

      • Mesosphere

      • Troposphere

      • Exosphere

      • Thermosphere

      • Stratosphere
fields.answer: Lowest: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Exosphere: Highest. All or nothing for points.

criteria.answer: Complete order, lowest to highest: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Exosphere. Published key says all or nothing.

fields.prompt: (2 points) Which layer of the atmosphere is the most dense, and why?
fields.answer: Troposphere, since it’s compressed by the layers above it.

criteria.answer: Troposphere is most dense
Compressed by the weight of atmospheric layers above it

fields.prompt: (3 points) For each layer of the atmosphere, what is the most common pollutant?
fields.answer: Troposphere: Particulate Matter (PM) (1pt); Stratosphere: Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS) (1pt); Mesosphere/Thermosphere/Exosphere: None (1pt). One point

criteria.answer: Troposphere: particulate matter (PM)
Stratosphere: ozone-depleting substances
Mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere: none

fields.answer: Accept any answer in the range 0.39◦−0.41◦

criteria.answer: 0.39° to 0.41° per day, as printed in the key

fields.prompt:
(2 points) Using your answer from the previous question, what would the longitude of the subsolar spot
   be on March 30th? Show your work.





   For question 6, write the appropriate instrument to monitor the atmospheric condition.
   There may be more than one correct answer, but there will be only one best answer.
fields.answer: The spring equinox is March 20th. March 30th is 10 days later. 10 days × 0.4◦= 4◦. In the spring, the sun is moving north, making the final position 4◦N. All or nothing points. For question 6, write the appropriate instrument to monitor the atmospheric condition. There may be more than one correct answer, but there will be only one best answer.
fields.context: The paper says ‘longitude’; the key expects 4° north of the equator on March 30.

criteria.answer: 4° north on March 30 using 10 days after March 20 at about 0.4° per day; all or nothing in key

fields.prompt:
For each listed atmospheric condition, name an appropriate monitoring instrument (0.5 point each): (6 points) Air temperature, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, wind speed, wind direction, precip-
    itation amount, cloud base height, solar radiation intensity, atmospheric ozone concentration, particulate
    matter, vertical temperature profile, and atmospheric water vapor content.
fields.answer: Air temperature (surface) — Thermometer Atmospheric pressure — Barometer Relative humidity — Hygrometer Wind speed — Anemometer Wind direction — Wind vane Precipitation amount — Rain gauge Cloud base height — Ceilometer Solar radiation intensity — Pyranometer Atmospheric ozone concentration — Dobson spectrophotometer Particulate matter (PM2.5 / PM10) — Air quality monitor Vertical temperature profile — Radiosonde Atmospheric water vapor content — Microwave radiometer. Award 0.5 points per correct

criteria.answer: Surface air temperature: thermometer
Atmospheric pressure: barometer
Relative humidity: hygrometer
Wind speed: anemometer
Wind direction: wind vane
Precipitation amount: rain gauge
Cloud-base height: ceilometer
Solar radiation intensity: pyranometer
Atmospheric ozone concentration: Dobson spectrophotometer
Particulate matter: air-quality monitor
Vertical temperature profile: radiosonde
Atmospheric water-vapor content: microwave radiometer

fields.prompt:
(2 points) Define and explain the meteorological significance of a wet-bulb temperature





                                        Page 2 of 5
Meteorology B                          Greenbrier Invitational              Team Number:
fields.answer: Wet-bulb temperature is the lowest temperature air can reach through evaporative cooling alone, under constant pressure. (1pt) It is important since it helps with the estimation of humidity, cloud formation, etc. (1pt)

criteria.answer: Wet-bulb temperature is the lowest air temperature achievable by evaporative cooling at constant pressure
Meteorological use: estimate humidity, cloud formation or related conditions

fields.prompt: (3 points) At the wet-bulb temperatures 0◦C, 10◦C, and 20◦C, what cloud formations would be expected
fields.answer: 0◦C: Nimbus/Stratonimbus (1pt) 10◦C: Cumulus (1pt) 20◦C Cumulonimbus (1pt)

criteria.answer: At 0°C: nimbus or nimbostratus/stratonimbus
At 10°C: cumulus
At 20°C: cumulonimbus

fields.prompt:
(2 points) What is the most important meteorological condition in order for a green flash to happen,
   and why?
fields.answer: A temperature inversion (1pt), because refraction and dispersion of sunlight is enhanced.

criteria.answer: A temperature inversion
It enhances refraction and dispersion of sunlight

fields.prompt:
(2 points) Compare and contrast mercury-based and alcohol-based thermometers based on their effec-
    tiveness at different temperatures
fields.answer: Mercury-based thermometers are better at measuring higher temperatures (1pt), whereas alcohol-based thermometers are better at lower temperatures (1pt).

criteria.answer: Mercury thermometers are better at higher temperatures
Alcohol thermometers are better at lower temperatures

fields.prompt: (2 points) Which region of the world has the most virga, and why?
fields.answer: The Great Basin (Nevada, US) (1pt), because of the high-elevation basins, extremely dry lower troposphere, frequent mid-level clouds, and precipitation aloft

criteria.answer: The Great Basin, Nevada, United States
Dry lower troposphere and high-elevation basins, with mid-level clouds or precipitation aloft

fields.prompt:
(2 points) If the Coriolis effect magically disappeared immediately, what would be expected over the
    course of the next five minutes?





                                        Page 3 of 5
Meteorology B                          Greenbrier Invitational              Team Number:


For questions 13-16, use the following information: On a summer afternoon, a weak surface
low and a nearby stationary front allow warm, moist air to pool over a flat inland region.
Daytime solar heating increases instability, producing scattered cumulus that grow into isolated
thunderstorms, but weak wind shear prevents storm organization. The storms produce brief
heavy rain and occasional lightning, with no hail or damaging winds.
fields.answer: If the Coriolis effect disappeared, surface winds would blow directly from high to low pressure without curving, trade winds and westerlies would vanish, cyclones and hurricanes could not rotate, ocean gyres would collapse, and precipitation and climate patterns worldwide would be drastically altered. Note to graders: this is supposed to be a more fun question before the more difficult scenario-based analysis ones, so please grade easier on this one.

criteria.answer: Without Coriolis deflection, surface winds move directly from high to low pressure instead of curving
One plausible short-term circulation change, such as trade/westerly wind pattern or cyclone rotation; grade generously per key

fields.prompt: (1 point) Identify the lifting mechanism responsible for thunderstorm initiation in this scenario.
fields.answer: Surface heating (convective lifting), aided by weak convergence along the stationary front.
fields.context: For questions 13–16: A summer afternoon has a weak surface low and nearby stationary front. Warm moist air pools over a flat inland region. Daytime heating produces isolated thunderstorms, but weak wind shear prevents organization. They bring brief heavy rain and lightning without hail or damaging winds.

criteria.answer: Surface heating causes convective lifting, aided by weak convergence along the stationary front

fields.prompt: (2 points) Explain why the thunderstorms remain nonsevere despite the presence of warm, moist air.
fields.answer: Although instability is present, weak vertical wind shear prevents storm organization and long-lived updrafts, limiting storm intensity.
fields.context: For questions 13–16: A summer afternoon has a weak surface low and nearby stationary front. Warm moist air pools over a flat inland region. Daytime heating produces isolated thunderstorms, but weak wind shear prevents organization. They bring brief heavy rain and lightning without hail or damaging winds.

criteria.answer: Weak vertical wind shear prevents organized storms
Updrafts do not persist long enough for severe intensity despite warm moist instability

fields.prompt:
(2 points) Describe how the vertical wind shear profile influences storm type and lifetime in this situa-
    tion.
fields.answer: Minimal vertical wind shear favors single-cell (air-mass) thunderstorms, where the downdraft quickly cuts off the updraft, resulting in short-lived storms.
fields.context: For questions 13–16: A summer afternoon has a weak surface low and nearby stationary front. Warm moist air pools over a flat inland region. Daytime heating produces isolated thunderstorms, but weak wind shear prevents organization. They bring brief heavy rain and lightning without hail or damaging winds.

criteria.answer: Minimal vertical shear favors single-cell or air-mass thunderstorms
Their downdrafts cut off updrafts, making storms short-lived

fields.prompt:
(3 points) If mid-level dry air were introduced into this environment, analyze how precipitation type
   and downdraft strength might change without necessarily producing severe storms.





                                        Page 4 of 5
Meteorology B                          Greenbrier Invitational              Team Number:


Use the following information to answer questions 17-20: As the single-cell thunderstorms
develop, they produce brief, localized heavy rain and occasional lightning strikes, but most
precipitation evaporates before reaching the ground in some areas. Gusty downdrafts cre-
ate temporary wind shifts at the surface, and minor puddling occurs in low-lying areas, but
no flooding develops. The storms quickly dissipate as the updraft collapses, leaving behind
scattered clouds and a temporary drop in temperature.
fields.answer: Dry mid-level air would enhance evaporational cooling, strengthening downdrafts and increasing gustiness, while precipitation may partially evaporate as virga or produce brief heavy rain, still without sufficient shear to become severe.
fields.context: For questions 13–16: A summer afternoon has a weak surface low and nearby stationary front. Warm moist air pools over a flat inland region. Daytime heating produces isolated thunderstorms, but weak wind shear prevents organization. They bring brief heavy rain and lightning without hail or damaging winds.

criteria.answer: Mid-level dry air causes more evaporation and evaporative cooling
Downdrafts strengthen and gustiness increases
Precipitation may evaporate as virga or briefly reach ground as heavy rain; weak shear can still prevent severe organization

fields.prompt:
(1 point) Identify what meteorological phenomenon is observed when precipitation evaporates before
    reaching the ground.
fields.answer: Virga
fields.context: For questions 17–20: These short-lived single-cell storms produce localized rain and lightning. Some precipitation evaporates before reaching the ground. Downdrafts cause temporary surface wind shifts and minor puddling; storms dissipate as updrafts collapse.

criteria.answer: Virga

fields.prompt: (2 points) Explain why surface gusts occur during these short-lived thunderstorms.
fields.answer: Gusts occur because downdrafts of cooler air from collapsing updrafts accelerate toward the surface, creating brief, localized wind events.
fields.context: For questions 17–20: These short-lived single-cell storms produce localized rain and lightning. Some precipitation evaporates before reaching the ground. Downdrafts cause temporary surface wind shifts and minor puddling; storms dissipate as updrafts collapse.

criteria.answer: Cooler-air downdrafts form as updrafts collapse
They accelerate to the surface and create short-lived localized gusts

fields.prompt: (2 points) Describe how uneven rainfall distribution in this scenario could impact local areas differently.
fields.answer: Some areas may receive brief heavy rain, causing temporary puddles, while others experience little or no surface rainfall due to virga, leading to unequal soil moisture and minor localized flooding.
fields.context: For questions 17–20: These short-lived single-cell storms produce localized rain and lightning. Some precipitation evaporates before reaching the ground. Downdrafts cause temporary surface wind shifts and minor puddling; storms dissipate as updrafts collapse.

criteria.answer: Some locations receive brief heavy rain and temporary puddles
Others get little or no surface rain due to virga, producing uneven soil moisture

fields.prompt:
(3 points) Analyze how the combination of virga and downdrafts affects near-surface temperature and
    humidity immediately after the storm.





                                        Page 5 of 5
fields.answer: Evaporation of falling precipitation (virga) cools and moistens the air aloft, while downdrafts push cooler, denser air to the surface, producing a temporary drop in temperature and a brief increase in local wind gusts, often followed by slightly increased surface humidity as the storm dissipates.
fields.context: For questions 17–20: These short-lived single-cell storms produce localized rain and lightning. Some precipitation evaporates before reaching the ground. Downdrafts cause temporary surface wind shifts and minor puddling; storms dissipate as updrafts collapse.

criteria.answer: Virga evaporates, cooling and moistening air aloft
Downdrafts bring cooler denser air down, temporarily lowering surface temperature and causing gusts
Surface humidity may rise slightly as the storm dissipates
